question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $2$nd row of our determinant is almost equal to the $3$rd row. So, we can rewrite the given determinant, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 9 \\ 202 & 203 & 205 \\ 202 & 203 & 204\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 9 \\ 202+0 & 203+0 & 204+1 \\ 202 & 203 & 204\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Next, using the linearity property of determinants, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 9 \\ 202+0 & 203+0 & 204+1 \\ 202 & 203 & 204\end{aligned}| & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 9 \\ 202 & 203 & 204 \\ 202 & 203 & 204\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 202 & 203 & 204\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

The first determinant must be zero since it has two identical rows, while the second determinant can be expanded across the $2$nd row, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 9 \\ 202 & 203 & 204 \\ 202 & 203 & 204\end{aligned}|+|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 202 & 203 & 204\end{aligned}| & =0+1(-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ 202 & 203\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(4\cdot 203-6\cdot 202) \\  & =-(812-1\,212) \\  & =400\end{aligned}
$$
